name: Melanoma
description: Melanoma is a serious type of skin cancer. It starts in pigment cells called melanocytes that give skin its color. It can spread quickly to other body organs if not found early.
common_symptoms: A mole that is changing size, shape, or color
One half of the spot does not match the other half (asymmetry)
Multiple colors in the same spot like black, brown, red, or white
A spot larger than a pencil eraser (wider than 6 mm)
A new spot that looks different from all your other moles (ugly duckling sign)
causes: DNA damage to skin cells caused by ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight or tanning lamps
Genetic factors and inherited gene mutations
risk_factors: Having fair skin that burns easily in the sun
History of severe sunburns, especially in childhood
Family history of melanoma or skin cancer
first_aid: Do not scratch, cut, squeeze, or apply home chemicals to the spot
Take a clear photo with a coin next to it to record the size and date
Cover the area with clothing to protect it from the sun
Book an urgent appointment with a dermatologist or doctor
precautions: Stay in the shade between 10 AM and 4 PM when the sun is strongest
Wear a wide hat, sunglasses, and long sleeves outdoors
Use broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every day
Check your skin from head to toe once every month
home_care: Keep the skin area clean and protected from rubbing
Avoid irritating the spot with harsh scrubs or tight waistbands
Do not attempt any home removal remedies
do_not: DO NOT try to scrape, cut, or burn off any mole at home
DO NOT use unproven herbal pastes, caustic creams, or wart removers
DO NOT wait to see if a changing dark spot goes away on its own
DO NOT ignore a spot because it does not hurt
red_flags: The spot bleeds, oozes, or forms a crust on its own
The spot grows rapidly in size or height within weeks
A new dark line appears under a fingernail or toenail without injury
The spot becomes painful, itchy, or swollen
when_to_see_doctor: See a dermatologist or doctor immediately if any mole changes color, shape, or size, has irregular edges, or bleeds.
prevention: Avoid sunburns and tanning beds completely
Apply SPF 30+ sunscreen 20 minutes before going outside
Have a doctor check your skin regularly if you have many moles
